foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Red Sea maritime disruption will sustain energy repricing pressure near 69% over 30 days, driven by 7 urgent critical signals reinforcing energy supply shock and headlines of Brent oil at $110 amid Iran-Hormuz...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 69% probability with 77% state confirmation and 7 urgent critical signals indicates a structurally reinforced energy supply shock path, with Brent at $110 serving as a market cue for sustained repricing.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level and lack of directly matched Red Sea reporting could prevent escalation, as actors may treat the current signals as noise rather than a durable trend, allowing stabilization toward 61%.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 69%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 69% pressure and 77% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
